question: Bowman's capsule encloses ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**the glomerulus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bowman’s capsules are found in the Kidney of Mammals.
 
• Bowman’s capsules is a cup-like sack at the nephron in the mammalian's kidney that performs the filtration of blood to form urine.
 
• The Bowman's capsule is a part of the excretion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Digestion

 
 
• Biomacromolecules in food cannot be utilized by our body in their original form.
 
• They have to be broken down and converted into simple substances in the digestive system.
 
• This process of conversion of complex food substances to simple absorbable forms is called digestion and is carried out by our digestive system by mechanical and biochemical methods.
 
 
 
• Respiration
 
 
• This process of exchange of O2 from the atmosphere with CO2 produced by the cells is called breathing, commonly known as respiration.
 
 
 
• The biological process involved in the removal of harmful metabolic wastes from the body is called excretion.
 
 
• Animals accumulate ammonia, urea, uric acid, carbon dioxide, water, and ions like Na+, K+, Cl–, phosphate, sulfate, etc., either by metabolic activities or by other means like excess ingestion.
 
• These substances have to be removed totally or partially. The mechanisms of elimination of these substances with special emphasis on common nitrogenous wastes.
 
• Ammonia, urea, and uric acid are the major forms of nitrogenous wastes excreted by animals.
